summary: The recorded base reproduced indefinite shallow-queue displacement of one cold request by continuous fresh hot arrivals. The exact candidate adds opt-in per-active-LPM-pass aging and bounded the same stream while preserving disabled behavior and the existing large-queue fallback.

tests.what_was_measured: On base, a cold request lost to 20 consecutive fresh requests with 100 matched tokens in a shallow queue; the aging constructor option was absent.
Candidate regression and adjacent unit coverage: 17 tests and 2 subtests passed.
Independent continuous-arrival bound, non-divisible ceil bounds, disabled ordering, 128/129 fallback boundary, CLI transport, negative validation, and source import paths.

gpu_execution.evidence: No GPU execution participates in the Python queue-ordering defect or candidate changes. The assigned single gfx950 cannot qualify the reported 8xB300 GLM-5.2-NVFP4 production workload.

remaining_limitations: The GLM-5.2-NVFP4 weights, 8xB300 topology, production traffic, and reported 20-60 second TTFT tail were not available, so production latency improvement was not reproduced.
A single gfx950 and tiny Llama fixture would validate neither the reported model architecture nor the distributed workload; they were not used as substitute proof.
No native source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
